LOCATION: a hallway outside a closed apartment door, the only light coming from under it
rehearsal room where the script stops two pages before the scene everyone remembers
drawing table covered in single parts, a hip socket here and a leg stump there, nothing joined yet
reading table with a 1952 letter under a magnifier and a legal pad of forty-one question marks
projection booth where the last reel is real footage of the night someone said nobody would believe it
ANTAGONIST: the question asked of a part, to someone who can only judge the whole
the error that points straight down the lens and so looks like no error
the scene planned so carefully that nothing is left to find
the confident word on page one before the book exists
MACGUFFIN: the full typed draft, every word guessed and something put in
the scene that isn't in the script
the second camera, fifty degrees around
the complete figure, head to feet, with one question attached
THREAT: asking someone for your job and keeping theirs for yourself
a fragment judged right that reads wrong once it is joined
the door stays shut and the fear stays in the hallway
the part checked only from the angle that made it
CHARACTER: the writer yelling his fears through a door at the old trainer on the other side
the patron who cannot read a word alone but knows her grandmother's voice in a sentence
the helper who stops asking 'barn or born?' and types the whole letter
the reader who says 'complete it and I can say if it reads'
